target_demo: 20-40 Korean adults; mobile-first users concerned with loans, interest rates and personal credit score
narrative_arc: Opens on a relatable pain point — a personal credit score that falls one point short when applying for a loan. A young adult studies her score on her phone; an editorial caption bar frames the feature as a 'one-touch cheat key' to raise your credit score. The ad then becomes a step-by-step in-app walkthrough shot as a flat-lay phone-on-orange screen demo: search the feature in the all-tab, open '신용점수 올리기', read what it does (auto-submits score-raising documents and reports the result), tap the raise button, watch the app find and submit documents, and land on the payoff — a celebratory score reveal (KCB 945, +54점 / NICE 950) — closing with a reminder to always check before applying for a loan. Series end card reveals 'Curator T / 토스를 발견하다'.

production_signature.signature_note: Two visual registers cut together: (1) warm shallow-DOF live-action interior shots of a Korean adult holding or studying an iPhone with the app on its screen, and (2) flat-lay top-down phone-on-vivid-orange screen-demo shots used for the step-by-step UI walkthrough. The walkthrough segments carry hardcoded lower-third caption bars (dark rounded pill, bold white Korean text) synced to the voiceover, while the live-action opening uses large centered white captions and a flat editorial 'CONTENT' header bar. The series end card is a distinctive pixel/CRT-distorted logo badge ('Curator T / 토스를 발견하다') with RGB chromatic-aberration text on a textured matte off-white paper field. Wiggle metric is low (mean_abs_shift_x 0.16) and confirmed visually: no stereoscopic parallax; interior shots are gentle handheld, flat-lay and end card are locked off.

analyst_notes: This entry is a screen-recording-style UI demo of a Korean fintech app's credit-score-raising feature, intercut with two warm live-action interior shots that establish the pain point. capture_style classified 'mixed' because shots 4-8 are flat-lay phone-on-orange screen-demo footage (effectively screen captures of the app composited onto an orange flat-lay) distinct from the live-action hand/woman shots (1-3).
